newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank chief sees bank rates easing.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank chief sees bank rates easing.

text.p: Thailand's central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday that he expects local commercial banks to cut their rates in the coming weeks.
"The central bank sees local commercial banks cutting deposit rates further in the next two to three weeks which will eventually lead to cuts in lending rates," he told reporters.

The governor said the interest rate might be cut by 25 basis points initially but will come down further, but he declined to say what level of interest rates would be deemed appropriate by the central bank.
"It depends on the market mechanism and the economic situation," Rerngchai said.
"Our economy is more stabilised now but concerns arise on the possibility of recession. If this continues, we will have to deal with more problems," he said.
Thailand's lending rates are among the highest in the region and range between 13 and 13.25 percent.
